additions.reason: The Torah explicitly states 'ha-aretz omedeth al amudim — hayna Binah, eretz ha-chayyim, she-mimenah totza'ot ha-tefillin.' Binah is the source from which tefillin shine forth (imma al bera). The Torah also cites 'im la-Binah tikra' as the basis for tefillin = imma al bera. Binah shares the essential nature of the tefillin-cluster as its root.
additions.source_quote: הָאָרֶץ עוֹמֶדֶת עַל עַמּוּדִים, הַיְנוּ בִּינָה, אֶרֶץ הַחַיִּים, שֶׁמִּמֶּנָּה תּוֹצְאוֹת הַתְּפִלִּין

additions.reason: The Torah section 5 states: 'tefillin nikra'in pe'er, she-ne'emar pe'erkha chavush alekha.' Pe'er is the essential name for tefillin and shares their nature — it is the glory/beauty that manifests as the totality of colors (klaliyut ha-gvanim) when shame appears on the face.
additions.source_quote: תְּפִלִּין נִקְרָאִין פְּאֵר, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: פְּאֶרְךָ חֲבוּשׁ עָלֶיךָ. וּפְאֵר הוּא כְּלָלִיּוּת הַגְּוָנִין

additions.reason: The Torah repeatedly identifies the metzach (forehead) as the primary locus of tefillin and the place where shame/bushah is revealed. 'Ikar hitgalut ha-bushah hi ba-metzach.' The forehead shares the essential nature of tefillin.
additions.source_quote: וְעִקַּר הִתְגַּלּוּת הַבּוּשָׁה הִיא בַּמֵּצַח, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (ירמיהו ג): וּמֵצַח אִשָּׁה זוֹנָה

additions.reason: The opening of the Torah states: 'kol adam tzarikh le-fashpesh et atzmo be-khol et im hu davuk ba-Shem yitbarakh. Ve-ha-siman shel devekut hu tefillin.' Devekut and tefillin share the same essential nature — tefillin IS the sign of devekut.
additions.source_quote: הַסִּימָן שֶׁל דְּבֵקוּת הוּא תְּפִלִּין, כִּי תְּפִלִּין הֵם סִימָן עַל הַדְּבֵקוּת

additions.reason: Section 6 cites the Zohar: 'va-yitnatzlu et edyam — da tefillin.' The edyam (ornaments stripped at Sinai) share the essential nature of tefillin in this Torah's framework.
The Torah explicitly states: 'ha-dibur nikra regel, ke-mo she-katuv: tzedek yikra'eihu le-raglo, u-khetuv: tzedek tedaberu.' Regel shares the essential nature of dibur.
additions.source_quote: כִּי הַדִּבּוּר נִקְרָא רֶגֶל, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (ישעיהו מא): צֶדֶק יִקְרָאֵהוּ לְרַגְלוֹ

additions.reason: Section 4d: 'ha-dibur nikra regel... bi-she'arayikh Yerushalayim — al yedei ha-Torah.' The Torah maps the gates of Jerusalem to dibur. In the cosmic stacking, the speech (dibur/yam) is elevated into Yerushalayim.
The Torah states: 've-rua'h se'arah ha-ze hu ha-mekatterg ha-gadol, she-mimenu ba'im kol ha-kitturgim ve-ha-nisyonot.' The great accuser shares the essential nature of ketz kol basar / rua'h se'arah.
additions.source_quote: וְרוּחַ סְעָרָה הַזֶּה הוּא מְקַטְרֵג הַגָּדוֹל, שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ בָּאִים כָּל הַקִּטְרוּגִים וְהַנִּסְיוֹנוֹת

additions.reason: Section 6: The Torah identifies azut panim as the opposite of tefillin-bushah. Adam ha-rishon pagam be-tefillin which led to azut-panim (gehinom). Azut panim = lack of bushah = absence of tefillin light. It is also identified with the pollution of the serpent (zuhmat ha-nachash) through the Cain narrative.

Section 3: 've-tzarikh le-ha'alot et ha-dibur le-shorshо, she-hu ha-zero'a, she-hem chamesh etzba'in she-be-yad smol, she-hem chamisha gevurot.' The zero'a (arm) shares the essential nature of the five gevurot / five fingers / five articulations of the mouth — they are all the same sefiratic dimension.
additions.source_quote: וְצָרִיךְ לְהַעֲלוֹת אֶת הַדִּבּוּר לְשָׁרְשׁוֹ, שֶׁהוּא הַזְּרוֹעַ, שֶׁהֵם חָמֵשׁ אֶצְבָּעִין שֶׁבְּיַד שְׂמֹאל

additions.reason: Section 5: 'shoresh ha-gevurot hem ba-lev... chamimut ha-lev.' The warmth of the heart is the root-expression of the gevurot, sharing their essential nature. It is the inner fire that powers the gevurot-speech.
additions.source_quote: שֹׁרֶשׁ הַגְּבוּרוֹת הֵם בַּלֵּב... חֲמִימוּת הַלֵּב

additions.reason: Section 7: 've-ha-luchot hem shoresh ha-Torah, ve-nikra'im y"o... ve-ikkar he'arat ha-tefillin ba'im al yedei ha-luchot.' The Tablets are the root of Torah, called yud-vav (16) which is the same number as the 16 horns. They are the source from which the tefillin-radiance comes, and share the nature of the gevurot (the Torah sharpens the intellect = the mochin = the luchot).
additions.source_quote: וְהַלּוּחוֹת הֵם שֹׁרֶשׁ הַתּוֹרָה, וְנִקְרָאִים י"ו, עַל־שֵׁם עֲשֶׂרֶת הַדִּבְּרוֹת

additions.reason: The Torah equates laylah with choshekh via the verse 've-la-choshekh kara layla.' Choshekh (darkness) shares the same essential nature as laylah in this Torah — it is the domain of ketz kol basar's dominion, the neutral condition of night-time distress.
additions.source_quote: שֶׁאָז שֻׁלְטְנוּתָא דְּקֵץ כָּל בָּשָׂר. כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: קֵץ שָׂם לַחֹשֶׁךְ, וּכְתִיב (בראשית א): וְלַחֹשֶׁךְ קָרָא לָיְלָה

additions.reason: The cosmic structure in section 7 describes 'amudim — bechina tefilah — al ha-mayim — haynu al ha-lev.' Water = heart, and the pillars (prayer) stand upon the heart. Lev shares the essential nature of tefilah in this Torah's cosmic stack.
additions.source_quote: וְעַמּוּדִים, בְּחִינַת תְּפִלָּה, עַל הַמַּיִם. הַיְנוּ עַל הַלֵּב

additions.reason: In the cosmic stack, 'amudim al ha-mayim — haynu al ha-lev.' Mayim = lev = the foundation upon which prayer stands. In this specific context the Torah explicitly equates them. A structural/neutral node.
additions.source_quote: עַל הַמַּיִם, הַיְנוּ עַל הַלֵּב, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: שִׁפְכִי כַמַּיִם לִבֵּךְ נֹכַח פְּנֵי ה'
